transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. I'm Dr. [Name], and I'll be speaking with you today. Can you tell me what brings you in — what's been going on that made you decide to come in for an evaluation?

Hello. ...Well, I suppose I'm having some trouble lately. In the evenings, mostly. 

It's, uh... it's with eating. Once I start eating at night, it's... it's strange. It feels almost like I can see myself doing it, and I'm telling myself to just stop, but... my hands just keep going back for more. 

That's... that's why I'm here.
Do you feel upset or distressed about this eating behavior, or has it been affecting your daily life in any way?

Well... I still manage my job. The work gets done, and I handle my responsibilities at the firm. 

But... I suppose it bothers me. I've been turning down plans lately. Things like my walking club, or... going to the theater with friends. I just... I don't really want people looking at me right now. I keep worrying they're going to think I've let myself go, or... that I don't look disciplined enough. 

It's a bit shameful, I guess. So I just stay home.

Can you describe what happens during these episodes of eating? Do you feel like you’re eating a much larger amount of food than most people would in one sitting, or that you’ve lost control over your eating during these times?

Well... yes. I suppose it is. 

I... I'll usually just start with some leftovers. But then I... I end up eating sandwiches, and cereal... cookies. Just whatever snack food is sitting in the pantry. It's... it's far more than I would ever put on a plate for a normal supper. 

So, yes, it's a lot. And... I already mentioned the part about feeling like my hands just keep going. I'd... rather not dwell on the details of it, to be honest.
Do these episodes of eating happen specifically during the night, after you've already gone to bed or in the middle of the night?
No, not usually. I... I haven't gone to bed yet when it happens. It's just in the evening, after work. I don't wake up to eat or anything like that.
Do these eating episodes cause you significant distress, such as feelings of guilt, embarrassment, or self-criticism afterward?

I... I wouldn't really use those words. 

I mean, I told you earlier that it's a bit shameful, but... I don't sit around feeling guilty or criticizing myself afterward. Once it's over, I just... I clean up the kitchen and move on. I prefer not to dwell on it.
When you're eating during these episodes, would you say you feel like you can't stop eating or control what or how much you're eating?

I... I thought I just went over this. But, yes. 

It's... it's like I said before. I can be standing there, watching myself do it, and in my head I'm telling myself to stop. But... my hands just keep reaching for more. I can't seem to make them quit until... well, until it's done.
After these episodes of eating, do you ever make yourself vomit, use laxatives, or exercise excessively to try to compensate for what you've eaten?

I don't... I don't make myself sick or take pills, no. 

I just... I try to balance it out, I suppose. If I have a bad night, I might just skip breakfast and lunch the next day. Or... I'll take a walk. Sometimes I'll walk a few miles past my usual route, even if my knees are acting up and I know I should probably head home. It just... it feels like I need to do something.
Have you been feeling down, hopeless, or losing interest in things you usually enjoy, especially around the time of these eating episodes?

No. I... I wouldn't say that. 

I still go to work, do my job... I haven't lost interest in my usual routine or anything like that. I'm not... hopeless. I just go about my day.
Do these evening eating episodes usually happen after a stressful or emotionally difficult day, or do they seem to happen regardless of how your day went?

I... I don't really know. 

I haven't paid that much attention to it. It just... it happens when it happens. I don't think it matters what kind of day it was.
How often do these evening eating episodes happen — are they something that occurs at least once a week, or less frequently?

I suppose... it's at least once a week. For the last several months, anyway. 

Most weeks, there's at least one night where I eat like that. And then... well, the next day I just spend my time trying to make up for it. You know, skipping meals, setting strict rules for myself about what I can have, or... taking that extra-long walk I mentioned. But yeah. At least once a week.
Do you ever feel anxious, upset, or emotionally overwhelmed specifically during or right after these evening eating episodes?

No... I don't think so. 

I'm not really one to get... emotionally overwhelmed. Like I said, it's just something that happens, and then it's done. I don't sit around feeling upset about it. I just focus on what I need to do the next day.
During these episodes, would you say that you feel a lack of control over your eating, like you can’t stop eating once you start?

I suppose... yeah. That's actually what brought me in. Once I start eating at night, it's... well. It feels like I can see myself doing it, and I'm telling myself to stop, but... my hands just keep going back for more. So, yes.
During these episodes, do you find yourself eating much more rapidly than usual?
I wouldn't say so. I don't really think I'm rushing through it or anything. It's... well, it's just a normal pace, I suppose. Just a lot of it.
Do these evening eating episodes happen even when you're not physically hungry, or do they usually occur when you feel like you genuinely need to eat?
I don't really know. I mean... I'm not paying attention to whether my stomach is growling or not. It's just... I get home, and it happens. I don't think about hunger.
Do you usually eat these evening meals alone, or do you try to hide the amount you're eating from others because you're embarrassed?
I'm usually just by myself. I don't... I wouldn't say I'm trying to hide it, if that's what you mean. It's just me in the kitchen.
During these evening eating episodes, do you find yourself eating until you feel uncomfortably full?
I don't really know. I guess I'm full, but... I don't really think about it being uncomfortable. It's just eating.
During these evening eating episodes, do you find yourself eating significantly faster than you normally would?
I don't... I haven't really noticed the speed. I just eat. I'm not timing myself or anything.

inference_history.note: Initial presentation of eating-related distress, possible lack of control around eating, and potential dissociation; differential includes binge eating disorder, anorexia nervosa, adjustment disorder with depressed mood, and unspecified depressive disorder.

Ruled out F32.9 (Major Depressive Disorder) because the patient denied feeling down, hopeless, or losing interest in usual activities. The eating episodes occur primarily in the evening with features of loss of control, which supports consideration of Binge Eating Disorder (F50.70) and Eating Disorder Not Otherwise Specified (F50.0). The presence of compensatory behaviors such as skipping meals and excessive walking suggests possible Bulimia Nervosa (F43.22).

Ruled out F43.22 (Adjustment disorder with mixed anxiety and depressed mood) due to absence of significant mood symptoms or emotional distress related to the eating episodes. Continued presence of key features of binge eating (loss of control, recurrent episodes, compensatory behaviors) supports retention of F50.70 and F50.0 as candidates.
